steps.title: Expansion pattern
steps.narration: Any difference squared expands to the sum of the squares minus twice the cross product.

steps.title: Match the radical term
steps.narration: Compare the cross term with twenty root thirty to find that the product of the two terms is ten root thirty.

steps.title: Check the rational sum
steps.narration: Squaring two root five gives twenty and squaring five root six gives one hundred and fifty, which add up to one hundred and seventy.

steps.title: Final expression
steps.narration: Therefore the number that squares to the given expression is two root five minus five root six.

teach.title: Recall the square identity
teach.narration: Because the target expression has a minus sign before the root, we write it as a minus b all squared.

teach.title: Identify the whole-number sum
teach.narration: The rational part comes from adding the two squares, so a squared plus b squared must equal one hundred and seventy.

teach.title: Halve the cross term
teach.narration: Divide twenty root thirty by two on both sides so we know the product of the two terms is ten root thirty.

teach.title: Split into two surds
teach.narration: Split ten into two times five and root thirty into root five times root six to form two root five and five root six.

teach.title: Expand to double check
teach.narration: Multiply out to check the squares: four times five is twenty and twenty-five times six is one hundred and fifty, giving one hundred and seventy.

teach.title: Final surd
teach.narration: Both the whole number part and the surd part match, so the number is two root five minus five root six.

steps.title: Read the diagram
steps.narration: From the figure, P Q is parallel to R S, angle P is sixty degrees, and the left angle at the crossing is one hundred degrees.

steps.title: Angle on a straight line
steps.narration: Subtract one hundred degrees from one hundred and eighty degrees to find the adjacent angle inside the upper triangle.

steps.title: Third angle in triangle
steps.narration: Use the angle sum of a triangle to find that angle Q is forty degrees.

steps.title: Alternate interior angle
steps.narration: Because P Q and R S are parallel, alternate interior angles are equal, so x is forty degrees.

teach.title: Read given angles
teach.narration: Start by reading the diagram: P Q is parallel to R S, angle P is sixty degrees, and the exterior angle on the left of the crossing is one hundred degrees.

teach.title: Angles on a straight line
teach.narration: The one hundred degree angle and the top angle at the crossing lie along straight line Q R, so they add to one hundred and eighty degrees, leaving eighty degrees.

teach.title: Angles in upper triangle
teach.narration: Now look at the upper triangle P O Q; the three interior angles of any triangle always add up to one hundred and eighty degrees.

teach.title: Find angle Q
teach.narration: Add sixty and eighty to get one hundred and forty, then subtract from one hundred and eighty to get forty degrees at Q.

teach.title: Alternate interior angles
teach.narration: Lines P Q and R S are parallel and cut by line Q R, forming a Z shape where alternate interior angles are equal.

teach.title: Value of x
teach.narration: Therefore angle x at R equals angle Q, which is forty degrees.

steps.title: Find total percentage
steps.narration: Adding a fifteen percent raise to the full original salary gives one hundred and fifteen percent.

steps.title: Set up equation
steps.narration: Write one hundred and fifteen percent as one point one five times the original salary S equal to three hundred and forty-five naira.

steps.title: Divide to find S
steps.narration: Divide both sides by one point one five to undo the increase and find S.

steps.title: Original monthly salary
steps.narration: The original monthly salary before the raise was three hundred naira.

teach.title: Combine percentages
teach.narration: Treat the unknown original salary as one hundred percent, so after a fifteen percent increase the new pay represents one hundred and fifteen percent.

teach.title: Write percentage equation
teach.narration: Express one hundred and fifteen percent of the original salary S as equal to three hundred and forty-five.

teach.title: Convert fraction to decimal
teach.narration: Divide one hundred and fifteen by one hundred to rewrite the multiplier neatly as one point one five.

teach.title: Divide both sides
teach.narration: Divide both sides by one point one five, which is the same as dividing thirty-four thousand five hundred by one hundred and fifteen, to get three hundred.

teach.title: Check the increase
teach.narration: Check by taking fifteen percent of three hundred, which is forty-five, and adding it back to three hundred to confirm we get three hundred and forty-five.

teach.title: Original salary
teach.narration: The original monthly salary is three hundred naira.

steps.title: Start dividing by 2
steps.narration: Divide thirty-nine by two to get nineteen remainder one, then divide nineteen by two to get nine remainder one.

steps.title: Divide down to zero
steps.narration: Keep dividing each quotient by two and recording each zero or one remainder until the quotient reaches zero.

steps.title: Read remainders upwards
steps.narration: Read the remainders from bottom to top to write the binary digits in order.

steps.title: Base two result
steps.narration: Thirty-nine in base ten equals one zero zero one one one in base two.

teach.title: First division by 2
teach.narration: To convert from base ten to base two, divide repeatedly by two and note every remainder; thirty-nine divided by two gives nineteen remainder one.

teach.title: Next two divisions
teach.narration: Divide nineteen by two to get nine remainder one, then divide nine by two to get four remainder one.

teach.title: Even quotients give zero
teach.narration: Because four and two are even, dividing by two leaves a remainder of zero each time.

teach.title: Final division
teach.narration: Divide one by two to get quotient zero and remainder one, which tells us to stop dividing.

teach.title: Collect remainders upward
teach.narration: The last remainder is the highest place value, so list the remainders from bottom to top as one zero zero one one one.

teach.title: Check with powers of 2
teach.narration: Check by adding the place values for the ones: thirty-two plus four plus two plus one equals thirty-nine.

teach.title: Base two number
teach.narration: So thirty-nine in base ten is one zero zero one one one in base two.

steps.title: Pentagon angle sum
steps.narration: Use n minus two times one hundred and eighty degrees with five sides to get five hundred and forty degrees.

steps.title: Sum the five angles
steps.narration: Let each equal angle be x, so four x plus the sixty-degree angle equals five hundred and forty degrees.

steps.title: Solve for x
steps.narration: Subtract sixty from both sides to get four hundred and eighty, then divide by four.

steps.title: Each equal angle
steps.narration: Each of the four equal interior angles measures one hundred and twenty degrees.

teach.title: Find total interior angles
teach.narration: A pentagon has five sides, so using the polygon angle sum formula gives three times one hundred and eighty, which is five hundred and forty degrees.

teach.title: Set up the equation
teach.narration: Call each of the four equal angles x; together with the fifth angle of sixty degrees, their sum must be five hundred and forty degrees.

teach.title: Subtract 60° from both sides
teach.narration: Subtract sixty degrees from both sides to isolate the four equal angles on the left.

teach.title: Divide both sides by 4
teach.narration: Divide four hundred and eighty degrees equally among the four equal angles to get one hundred and twenty degrees.

teach.title: Verify the angle sum
teach.narration: Check by adding four angles of one hundred and twenty degrees plus sixty degrees, which gives five hundred and forty degrees.

teach.title: Final angle
teach.narration: Each of the four equal angles is one hundred and twenty degrees.

steps.title: Sector area formula
steps.narration: When radius and arc length are known, sector area equals one half times radius times arc length.

steps.title: Substitute given lengths
steps.narration: Multiply one half by seven and six to compute the area directly.

steps.title: Area of sector
steps.narration: The area of the sector is twenty-one square centimetres.

teach.title: List given dimensions
teach.narration: Write down the two measurements from the question: radius r is seven centimetres and arc length l is six centimetres.

teach.title: Relate area to arc length
teach.narration: Just like the area of a triangle is half base times height, a sector area is one half times radius times arc length, without needing the angle.

teach.title: Substitute r and l
teach.narration: Put seven in place of r and six in place of l into the formula.

teach.title: Multiply and halve
teach.narration: Take half of six to get three, then multiply three by seven to get twenty-one.

teach.title: Final sector area
teach.narration: Since the lengths are in centimetres, the area of the sector is twenty-one square centimetres.

steps.title: Original total age
steps.narration: Multiply thirty pupils by the old mean of fifteen point three to find the original total age.

steps.title: New total age
steps.narration: Multiply thirty pupils by the new mean of fifteen point two because the class size stays at thirty.

steps.title: Find age difference
steps.narration: Subtract the new total from the old total to see how much older the boy is than the girl.

steps.title: Age difference
steps.narration: The boy is three years older than the girl.

teach.title: Link mean and total
teach.narration: Remember that total age equals the number of pupils multiplied by their mean age.

teach.title: Compute initial total
teach.narration: Multiply thirty by fifteen point three to get four hundred and fifty-nine years for the original group.

teach.title: Compute new total
teach.narration: One pupil leaves and one joins, so there are still thirty pupils; thirty times fifteen point two gives four hundred and fifty-six years.

teach.display: Boy − Girl = Old total − New total
teach.title: Compare the two totals
teach.narration: All other twenty-nine pupils stayed the same, so the drop in total age equals the boy's age minus the girl's age.

teach.title: Subtract the totals
teach.narration: Subtract four hundred and fifty-six from four hundred and fifty-nine to get a difference of three.

teach.title: How much older
teach.narration: Therefore the boy is three years older than the girl.

steps.title: Set up tangent ratio
steps.narration: In the right-angled triangle, tangent of thirty degrees equals the building height divided by horizontal distance d.

steps.title: Use exact tan 30°
steps.narration: Replace tangent of thirty degrees with its exact surd value one over root three.

steps.title: Cross-multiply for d
steps.narration: Cross-multiply so d stands alone on one side.

steps.title: Horizontal distance
steps.narration: The instrument is forty root three metres horizontally from the building.

teach.title: Identify triangle sides
teach.narration: The forty-metre building is opposite the thirty-degree angle of elevation, and the ground distance d we want is the adjacent side.

teach.title: Write tangent formula
teach.narration: Because we have opposite and adjacent sides, use tangent equals opposite over adjacent.

teach.title: Substitute tan 30°
teach.narration: From special triangle values, tangent of thirty degrees is one over root three.

teach.title: Cross-multiply
teach.narration: Multiply diagonally so d times one equals forty times root three.

teach.title: Check size
teach.narration: Since thirty degrees is less than forty-five degrees, the ground distance must exceed forty metres, and forty root three is roughly sixty-nine metres.

teach.title: Final distance
teach.narration: The horizontal distance from the building is forty root three metres.

steps.title: Split outer and inner
steps.narration: Identify the inside polynomial as u and the outside function as cosine of u.

steps.title: Differentiate both parts
steps.narration: Differentiate cosine u to get minus sine u, and differentiate three x squared minus two x to get six x minus two.

steps.title: Multiply by chain rule
steps.narration: Multiply the two derivatives together and replace u with three x squared minus two x.

steps.title: Final derivative
steps.narration: The derivative is minus open bracket six x minus two close bracket times sine of three x squared minus two x.

teach.title: Define inner expression
teach.narration: Because cosine acts on a quadratic expression instead of just x, apply the chain rule by calling the inside expression u.

teach.title: Differentiate the outer cosine
teach.narration: The derivative of cosine u with respect to u is minus sine u, keeping the inner argument untouched.

teach.title: Differentiate the inner function
teach.narration: Differentiate three x squared minus two x term by term using the power rule to get six x minus two.

teach.title: State the chain rule
teach.narration: By the chain rule, multiply the derivative of the outer function by the derivative of the inner function.

teach.title: Substitute u back in
teach.narration: Put three x squared minus two x back inside sine and write the algebraic factor in front so it is not mixed into the angle.

teach.title: Derivative with respect to x
teach.narration: The derivative is minus open bracket six x minus two close bracket times sine of three x squared minus two x.

steps.title: Relate 5 to 10
steps.narration: Write five as ten divided by two so we can use the given value for log base eight of ten.

steps.title: Split the logarithm
steps.narration: By the quotient law of logarithms, dividing inside becomes subtracting two logarithms.

steps.title: Evaluate log base 8 of 2
steps.narration: Since two is the cube root of eight, log base eight of two equals one third.

steps.title: Expression in terms of x
steps.narration: Substituting x gives x minus one third.

teach.title: Express 5 using 10 and 2
teach.narration: We are given log base eight of ten, so write five as ten divided by two to connect it to ten.

teach.title: Apply logarithm quotient law
teach.narration: The logarithm of a quotient equals the logarithm of the numerator minus the logarithm of the denominator.

teach.title: Substitute x for log 10
teach.narration: Replace log base eight of ten with x as defined in the question.

teach.title: Write 2 as a power of 8
teach.narration: Because eight equals two cubed, taking the cube root of both sides shows that two is eight to the power one third.

teach.title: Read off the logarithm
teach.narration: By the definition of logarithms, log base eight of eight to the one third is simply one third.

teach.title: Final expression
teach.narration: Substituting one third gives log base eight of five equal to x minus one third.

steps.title: Equal roots condition
steps.narration: A quadratic equation has equal roots when its discriminant equals zero.

steps.title: Substitute coefficients
steps.narration: Put a equals one, b equals minus open bracket p minus two close bracket, and c equals two p plus one into the discriminant.

steps.title: Expand and factorise
steps.narration: Expand and simplify to p squared minus twelve p equals zero, then factor out p.

steps.title: Values of p
steps.narration: Setting each factor to zero gives p equals zero or twelve.

teach.title: Read a, b, and c
teach.narration: Compare the equation with a x squared plus b x plus c equals zero to read off the three coefficients.

teach.title: Condition for equal roots
teach.narration: For a quadratic to have two equal roots, the discriminant b squared minus four a c must equal zero.

teach.title: Substitute into discriminant
teach.narration: Substitute the coefficients; squaring the negative sign makes the first term p minus two all squared.

teach.title: Expand both brackets
teach.narration: Expand p minus two all squared to p squared minus four p plus four, and distribute minus four over two p plus one.

teach.title: Combine like terms and factor
teach.narration: The plus four and minus four cancel out, leaving p squared minus twelve p equals zero, which factors as p times p minus twelve.

teach.title: Solve each factor
teach.narration: Equate each factor to zero to get p equals zero or p equals twelve.

teach.title: Check p = 12
teach.narration: Quick check: when p is twelve, the equation becomes x minus five all squared equals zero, confirming equal roots.

teach.title: Final values of p
teach.narration: Therefore the required values of p are zero and twelve.

steps.title: Count all bottles
steps.narration: Add ten Coca-Cola, eight Fanta, and six Sprite bottles to get twenty-four bottles in total.

steps.title: Count non-Coca-Cola bottles
steps.narration: Any Fanta or Sprite bottle is not Coca-Cola, giving fourteen favourable bottles.

steps.title: Divide and reduce
steps.narration: Divide fourteen by twenty-four and cancel two from top and bottom.

steps.title: Required probability
steps.narration: The probability that the bottle is not Coca-Cola is seven over twelve.

teach.title: State probability formula
teach.narration: Because every bottle is equally likely, probability equals the number of favourable outcomes divided by the total number of outcomes.

teach.title: Find total bottles
teach.narration: Add all the bottles in the crate: ten plus eight plus six equals twenty-four.

teach.title: Count Fanta and Sprite
teach.narration: Not Coca-Cola means picking either Fanta or Sprite, so add eight and six to get fourteen bottles.

teach.title: Form probability fraction
teach.narration: Place the fourteen favourable bottles over the twenty-four total bottles.

teach.title: Simplify the fraction
teach.narration: Divide both numerator and denominator by their common factor two to simplify the fraction.

teach.title: Final probability
teach.narration: The probability that the chosen bottle is not Coca-Cola is seven twelfths.

steps.display: (\cos q − \sin q)^{2} = \cos^{2} q − 2 \sin q \cos q + \sin^{2} q
steps.title: Expand the square
steps.narration: Expand the bracket into cosine squared minus two sine cosine plus sine squared.

steps.title: Apply trig identities
steps.narration: Use sine squared plus cosine squared equals one, and two sine q cosine q equals sine two q.

steps.title: Differentiate with respect to q
steps.narration: The constant one differentiates to zero, and differentiating minus sine two q gives minus two cosine two q.

steps.title: Final derivative
steps.narration: The derivative with respect to q is minus two cosine two q.

teach.title: Expand the squared bracket
teach.narration: Expanding the bracket first makes the expression simpler to differentiate using standard trig identities.

teach.title: Use Pythagorean identity
teach.narration: Group cosine squared q plus sine squared q together and replace their sum with one.

teach.title: Use double-angle formula
teach.narration: Replace two sine q cosine q with sine two q so the expression becomes one minus sine two q.

teach.title: Differentiate the constant
teach.narration: The derivative of the constant one is zero.

teach.title: Differentiate sine 2q
teach.narration: By the chain rule, sine two q differentiates to cosine two q multiplied by two from the inner angle.

teach.title: Derivative result
teach.narration: Therefore the derivative is minus two cosine two q.

steps.title: Factorise quadratic
steps.narration: Find two numbers multiplying to minus twelve and adding to minus one: minus four and plus three.

steps.title: Find boundary values
steps.narration: Set each factor to zero to get boundary points minus three and four.

steps.title: Test between roots
steps.narration: Testing x equals zero gives a negative value, so the expression is non-negative outside the roots.

steps.title: Solution set
steps.narration: Include the boundary roots because of the greater-than-or-equal sign, giving x less than or equal to minus three or x greater than or equal to four.

teach.title: Write the inequality
teach.narration: We want all real numbers x where x squared minus x minus twelve is greater than or equal to zero.

teach.title: Factorise the left side
teach.narration: Since minus four times three is minus twelve and minus four plus three is minus one, factor the quadratic as x minus four times x plus three.

teach.title: Find critical points
teach.narration: The product changes sign only at the values where each bracket is zero, namely minus three and four.

teach.title: Test inside the interval
teach.narration: Test x equals zero between minus three and four; minus twelve is negative, so this middle interval fails the inequality.

teach.title: Test outer intervals
teach.narration: Because the x squared coefficient is positive, the quadratic rises above zero to the left of minus three and to the right of four.

teach.title: Include endpoints
teach.narration: At minus three and four the expression equals zero, which satisfies greater than or equal to, so x is at most minus three or at least four.

steps.title: Add servicing cost
steps.narration: Add the purchase cost and servicing cost to get thirty-six thousand naira total cost.

steps.title: Calculate 15% profit
steps.narration: Find fifteen percent of thirty-six thousand naira to get five thousand four hundred naira.

steps.title: Add profit to total cost
steps.narration: Add the profit to the total cost to obtain the selling price.

steps.title: Selling price
steps.narration: The selling price of the photocopier is forty-one thousand four hundred naira.

teach.title: Combine all costs
teach.narration: Profit is calculated on total cost, so add the two thousand naira servicing fee to the thirty-four thousand naira price first.

teach.title: Write 15% of total cost
teach.narration: Express fifteen percent profit on total cost as fifteen hundredths multiplied by thirty-six thousand.

teach.title: Calculate profit amount
teach.narration: Cancel two zeros from thirty-six thousand and one hundred, then multiply fifteen by three hundred and sixty to get five thousand four hundred naira.

teach.title: Add profit to total cost
teach.narration: Add the five thousand four hundred naira profit onto the thirty-six thousand naira total cost.

teach.title: Final selling price
teach.narration: The photocopier sells for forty-one thousand four hundred naira.

steps.title: Sphere surface area
steps.narration: Set the sphere surface area formula four pi r squared equal to one hundred and fifty-four.

steps.title: Substitute \frac{22}{7} for π
steps.narration: Substitute twenty-two over seven for pi because one hundred and fifty-four is divisible by twenty-two.

steps.title: Solve and take square root
steps.narration: Rearrange for r squared to get forty-nine over four, then take the positive square root.

steps.title: Radius of sphere
steps.narration: Seven divided by two gives a radius of three point five zero centimetres.

teach.title: State sphere area formula
teach.narration: Recall that the total curved surface area of a sphere of radius r is four pi r squared.

teach.title: Equate to 154 with pi
teach.narration: Substitute one hundred and fifty-four for the area and twenty-two sevenths for pi.

teach.title: Combine the constant factors
teach.narration: Multiply four by twenty-two over seven to write the coefficient neatly as eighty-eight over seven.

teach.title: Isolate r squared
teach.narration: Multiply both sides by seven and divide by eighty-eight; dividing both one hundred fifty-four and eighty-eight by twenty-two simplifies this to forty-nine over four.

teach.title: Take the positive root
teach.narration: Since a radius is positive, take the square root of forty-nine over four to get seven over two, or three point five zero.

teach.title: Radius to 0.01 cm
teach.narration: To two decimal places, the radius of the sphere is three point five zero centimetres.

steps.title: First term and difference
steps.narration: Identify the arithmetic progression with first term five and common difference six.

steps.title: Series sum formula
steps.narration: Write the standard formula for the sum of the first n terms of an arithmetic progression.

steps.title: Substitute and simplify
steps.narration: Substitute five for a and six for d, then simplify inside the bracket to six n plus four.

steps.title: Sum of n terms
steps.narration: Dividing six n plus four by two gives n times open bracket three n plus two close bracket.

teach.title: Check constant difference
teach.narration: Each term increases by six from the previous term, so this is an arithmetic progression with first term five and common difference six.

teach.title: State sum formula
teach.narration: Recall the sum formula for an arithmetic series: n over two times two a plus n minus one times d.

teach.title: Plug in a and d
teach.narration: Substitute five for a and six for d inside the brackets.

teach.title: Simplify inside brackets
teach.narration: Multiply six across n minus one to get six n minus six, then combine ten and minus six to get four.

teach.title: Divide bracket by 2
teach.narration: Multiply the factor one half into six n plus four to get three n plus two.

teach.title: Check for n = 2
teach.narration: Test n equals two: two times eight is sixteen, which matches five plus eleven.

teach.title: Final sum formula
teach.narration: So the sum of the first n terms is n times three n plus two.

steps.title: One man, two women
steps.narration: Choose one man from five and two women from three, giving five times three equals fifteen ways.

steps.title: Two men, one woman
steps.narration: Choose two men from five and one woman from three, giving ten times three equals thirty ways.

steps.title: Add both cases
steps.narration: Because the two compositions cannot happen together, add fifteen and thirty.

steps.title: Possible delegations
steps.narration: There are forty-five possible delegations.

teach.title: List allowed compositions
teach.narration: A delegation of three with at least one man and one woman can only have one man and two women, or two men and one woman.

teach.title: Combination formula
teach.narration: Order inside a delegation does not matter, so use combinations for each selection.

teach.title: Count 1 man and 2 women
teach.narration: Five choose one is five and three choose two is three; multiply them together to get fifteen ways.

teach.title: Evaluate 5 choose 2
teach.narration: Calculate five choose two as five times four divided by two, which is ten.

teach.title: Count 2 men and 1 woman
teach.narration: Multiply ten ways to pick two men by three ways to pick one woman to get thirty ways.

teach.title: Add disjoint cases
teach.narration: Add the counts from the two separate cases: fifteen plus thirty equals forty-five.

teach.title: Total delegations
teach.narration: Altogether, forty-five delegations can be formed.

steps.display: TS = 10 cm, SR = 8 cm, Area(△QRS) = 20 cm^{2}
steps.title: Read the diagram
steps.narration: From the diagram, T S is ten centimetres, S R is eight centimetres, and triangle Q R S has area twenty square centimetres.

steps.title: Find shared height
steps.narration: Use the triangle area formula with base eight centimetres to find a perpendicular height of five centimetres.

steps.title: Area of parallelogram
steps.narration: The parallelogram has base ten centimetres and the same height five centimetres, giving fifty square centimetres.

steps.title: Area of trapezium PQRT
steps.narration: Adding fifty and twenty gives seventy square centimetres for trapezium P Q R T.

teach.display: TS = 10 cm, SR = 8 cm, Area(△QRS) = 20 cm^{2}
teach.title: Read figure dimensions
teach.narration: Read the labels off the figure: base T S of the parallelogram is ten centimetres, base S R of the triangle is eight centimetres, and the triangle area is twenty.

teach.title: Use triangle area formula
teach.narration: Substitute base eight centimetres and area twenty into half base times height to find the perpendicular height h.

teach.title: Divide both sides by 4
teach.narration: Half of eight is four, so divide twenty by four on both sides to get height h equals five centimetres.

teach.title: Find parallelogram area
teach.narration: Because P Q is parallel to baseline T R, parallelogram P Q S T has the same perpendicular height five centimetres, so multiply ten by five.

teach.title: Add the two regions
teach.narration: Trapezium P Q R T is made of parallelogram P Q S T plus triangle Q R S, so add fifty and twenty.

teach.title: Check with trapezium rule
teach.narration: Check using the trapezium formula: half the sum of parallel sides ten and eighteen times height five also equals seventy.

teach.title: Area of PQRT
teach.narration: The area of trapezium P Q R T is seventy square centimetres.

steps.title: Gradient function
steps.narration: The gradient at every point gives the derivative d y by d x equal to six x minus five.

steps.title: Integrate to find y
steps.narration: Integrate six x minus five with respect to x, remembering to include the constant of integration C.

steps.title: Use point (2, 5) for C
steps.narration: Substitute x equals two and y equals five to find that C equals three.

steps.title: Equation of the curve
steps.narration: Putting C back gives y equals three x squared minus five x plus three.

teach.title: Write gradient equation
teach.narration: The gradient of a curve is its derivative d y by d x, so we start with d y by d x equals six x minus five.

teach.title: Integrate term by term
teach.narration: Use the reverse power rule to integrate six x to three x squared and minus five to minus five x, plus an unknown constant C.

teach.title: Substitute (2, 5)
teach.narration: Since the curve passes through two comma five, replace x with two and y with five to solve for C.

teach.title: Evaluate the numbers
teach.narration: Three times four is twelve and five times two is ten, leaving two plus C equals five.

teach.title: Subtract 2 from both sides
teach.narration: Subtract two from both sides so C equals three.

teach.title: Check point and gradient
teach.narration: Checking x equals two gives y equals five, and differentiating gives six x minus five.

teach.title: Curve equation
teach.narration: The equation of the curve is y equals three x squared minus five x plus three.

steps.title: Compute P squared
steps.narration: Multiply matrix P by itself row by column to get first row one, two, and second row minus six, minus three.

steps.title: Subtract 2P
steps.narration: Multiply P by two and subtract each entry from P squared to leave minus three down the main diagonal and zeros elsewhere.

steps.title: Add 4I
steps.narration: Add four times the identity matrix so each diagonal entry goes from minus three to one.

steps.title: Resulting matrix
steps.narration: The value of P squared minus two P plus four I is the two by two identity matrix, first row one, zero, second row zero, one.

teach.title: Set up matrix square
teach.narration: Write P squared as matrix P multiplied by itself; do not just square each entry individually.

teach.title: Multiply rows by columns
teach.narration: Compute each entry by pairing a row from the first matrix with a column from the second matrix.

teach.title: Find 2P
teach.narration: Multiply every entry of P by two to form two P.

teach.title: Subtract entry by entry
teach.narration: Subtract two P from P squared; notice both off-diagonal entries become zero.

teach.title: Write 4I
teach.narration: Multiply the two by two identity matrix by four, placing four on the main diagonal.

teach.title: Add 4I
teach.narration: Add four to minus three on each diagonal entry, giving ones on the diagonal.

teach.title: Final matrix
teach.narration: The result is the two by two identity matrix with ones on the main diagonal and zeros elsewhere.

steps.title: Find both slopes
steps.narration: Rearrange both equations into y equals m x plus c form so we can read off their slopes.

steps.title: Perpendicular slope rule
steps.narration: Because the lines are perpendicular, the product of their slopes must equal minus one.

steps.title: Solve for a
steps.narration: Multiply the two slopes and set their product equal to minus one.

steps.title: Value of a
steps.narration: Multiplying both sides by minus eight gives a equals eight.

teach.title: Make y subject of line 1
teach.narration: Move minus a x and plus four to the right side, then divide both sides by two so the coefficient of x gives the first slope a over two.

teach.title: Make y subject of line 2
teach.narration: Rearrange the second equation to y equals minus one quarter x plus one, so its slope is minus one quarter.

teach.title: Condition for perpendicularity
teach.narration: Two non-vertical lines are perpendicular when multiplying their slopes gives minus one.

teach.title: Multiply the slopes
teach.narration: Multiply the numerators and denominators to get minus a over eight equal to minus one.

teach.title: Multiply both sides by −8
teach.narration: Multiply both sides by minus eight so a stands alone on the left.

teach.title: Verify slope product
teach.narration: Checking a equals eight gives slope four, and four times minus one quarter equals minus one.

teach.title: Final value of a
teach.narration: The value of a is eight.

steps.title: Write linear factors
steps.narration: For each zero r, form the linear factor x minus r, giving x plus two, x plus one, and x minus three.

steps.title: Multiply first pair
steps.narration: Multiply x plus two by x plus one to get x squared plus three x plus two.

steps.title: Multiply by (x − 3)
steps.narration: Distribute x and minus three across the quadratic bracket.

steps.title: Simplified cubic
steps.narration: The x squared terms cancel out, leaving x cubed minus seven x minus six.

teach.title: Form factors from zeros
teach.narration: By the factor theorem, if r is a zero then x minus r is a factor, so subtracting minus two and minus one flips their signs to plus.

teach.title: Expand the first two factors
teach.narration: Multiply the first two brackets first and combine x and two x into three x.

teach.title: Multiply by the third factor
teach.narration: Now multiply this quadratic expression by the third factor x minus three.

teach.title: Distribute each term
teach.narration: Multiply every term inside by x, then multiply every term inside by minus three.

teach.title: Collect like terms
teach.narration: Plus three x squared and minus three x squared cancel, while two x minus nine x gives minus seven x.

teach.title: Test a zero
teach.narration: Substitute x equals three: twenty-seven minus twenty-one minus six equals zero as required.

teach.title: Cubic polynomial
teach.narration: The polynomial with those three zeros is x cubed minus seven x minus six.

steps.title: Combine both divisors
steps.narration: An integer divisible by both two and three must be divisible by their least common multiple, six.

steps.title: List favourable integers
steps.narration: From one through twenty, there are three multiples of six: six, twelve, and eighteen.

steps.title: Apply probability formula
steps.narration: Divide three favourable integers by the twenty integers in total.

steps.title: Required probability
steps.narration: The probability that the selected integer is divisible by both two and three is three over twenty.

teach.title: State probability formula
teach.narration: Because every integer from one to twenty has an equal chance, probability is the count of favourable integers over the total count.

teach.title: Count total integers
teach.narration: There are twenty possible integers in the sample space from one through twenty.

teach.title: Find least common multiple
teach.narration: To be divisible by both two and three at once, a number must be a multiple of six.

teach.title: List qualifying integers
teach.narration: The multiples of six up to twenty are six, twelve, and eighteen; twenty-four is too large, so only three integers qualify.

teach.title: Compute probability
teach.narration: Place the three qualifying integers over the twenty total integers.

teach.title: Final probability
teach.narration: Since three and twenty share no common factor other than one, the probability is three twentieths.

steps.title: Find sale price each
steps.narration: A twenty-five percent loss means each goat sells for seventy-five percent of four thousand naira, which is three thousand naira.

steps.title: Divide total proceeds
steps.narration: Divide the total sales of one hundred and eighty thousand naira by three thousand naira per goat.

steps.title: Number of goats
steps.narration: The trader bought sixty goats.

teach.title: Remaining percentage
teach.narration: Selling at a twenty-five percent loss means the trader receives seventy-five percent of the cost price.

teach.title: Sale price per goat
teach.narration: Take three quarters of four thousand naira to find that each goat sold for three thousand naira.

teach.title: Set up division
teach.narration: Divide the total money received from all goats by the selling price of one goat.

teach.title: Cancel zeros and divide
teach.narration: Cancel three zeros from top and bottom, then divide one hundred and eighty by three to get sixty.

teach.title: Check total loss
teach.narration: Check: sixty goats cost two hundred and forty thousand naira, and subtracting a twenty-five percent loss of sixty thousand leaves one hundred and eighty thousand.

teach.title: Total goats bought
teach.narration: The trader bought sixty goats.

steps.title: Expand along row 1
steps.narration: Expand across the top row with alternating plus, minus, plus signs.

steps.title: Evaluate 2 × 2 minors
steps.narration: Evaluate each two by two determinant using main diagonal minus other diagonal.

steps.title: Multiply terms out
steps.narration: Multiply each entry by its minor; note minus five times minus four gives plus twenty.

steps.title: Determinant of N
steps.narration: Adding twenty-one and twenty gives forty-one, and subtracting twenty-four gives seventeen.

teach.title: Set cofactor signs
teach.narration: When expanding a three by three determinant across the first row, the three terms carry signs plus, minus, and plus.

teach.title: Write the three minors
teach.narration: For each first-row number, cross out its row and column to form the remaining two by two determinant.

teach.title: Evaluate first minor
teach.narration: In the first minor, minus three times one is minus three, and subtracting minus ten adds ten to give seven.

teach.title: Evaluate second minor
teach.narration: In the second minor, six times one is six, and minus five times minus two is positive ten, so six minus ten is minus four.

teach.title: Evaluate third minor
teach.narration: In the third minor, six times two is twelve, and minus three times minus two is six, leaving twelve minus six equal to six.

teach.title: Combine the three terms
teach.narration: Watch the double minus sign on minus five times minus four, which makes plus twenty; twenty-one plus twenty minus twenty-four gives seventeen.

teach.title: Final determinant
teach.narration: The determinant of matrix N is seventeen.

steps.title: Multiply by conjugate
steps.narration: Multiply numerator and denominator by three plus root five, the conjugate of the denominator.

steps.title: Simplify denominator
steps.narration: Difference of squares clears the root in the denominator to give nine minus five equals four.

steps.title: Expand numerator
steps.narration: Expand the top brackets and combine six minus five to one, and two root five minus three root five to minus root five.

steps.title: Rationalised fraction
steps.narration: The rationalised expression is one minus root five all over four.

teach.title: Identify the conjugate
teach.narration: To remove the surd from three minus root five, flip the middle sign to get its conjugate, three plus root five.

teach.title: Multiply top and bottom
teach.narration: Multiply both top and bottom by three plus root five so the overall value of the fraction stays unchanged.

teach.title: Difference of squares
teach.narration: The denominator is a difference of two squares, so it simplifies cleanly to nine minus five, which is four.

teach.title: Expand the numerator
teach.narration: Multiply each term of the first bracket by three plus root five.

teach.title: Collect like terms
teach.narration: Combine the whole numbers six minus five to get one, and combine two root five minus three root five to get minus root five.

teach.title: Final rationalised form
teach.narration: Put the numerator over the denominator four to get one minus root five over four.

steps.title: Find y at x = 2
steps.narration: Plug x equals two into the second graph to find the y value where the two curves meet.

steps.title: Substitute into first curve
steps.narration: Substitute x equals two and y equals seven into y equals p x squared plus q.

steps.title: Make p the subject
steps.narration: Subtract q from both sides, then divide both sides by four.

steps.title: p in terms of q
steps.narration: Therefore p equals seven minus q all over four.

teach.title: Find y from second graph
teach.narration: Because both graphs pass through the same point at x equals two, first evaluate the known curve at x equals two to get y equals seven.

teach.title: Plug (2, 7) into first curve
teach.narration: The point two comma seven also lies on the first curve, so substitute x equals two and y equals seven.

teach.title: Simplify two squared
teach.narration: Two squared is four, giving four p plus q equals seven.

teach.title: Subtract q from both sides
teach.narration: Subtract q from both sides so the term containing p is on its own.

teach.title: Divide both sides by 4
teach.narration: Divide both sides by four to express p in terms of q.

teach.title: Final expression for p
teach.narration: So p in terms of q is seven minus q over four.

steps.title: Evaluate top logarithms
steps.narration: Three cubed is twenty-seven, and one quarter to the minus three is sixty-four, so the two top logs are three and minus three.

steps.title: Evaluate bottom logarithm
steps.narration: Since one over eighty-one is three to the minus four, the denominator log is minus four.

steps.title: Combine into fraction
steps.narration: Three minus negative three adds to six, divided by minus four.

steps.title: Simplified value
steps.narration: Dividing top and bottom by two simplifies the answer to minus three halves.

teach.title: Evaluate log base 3 of 27
teach.narration: Ask what power of three gives twenty-seven; since three cubed is twenty-seven, the first log equals three.

teach.title: Evaluate \log_{\frac{1}{4}} 64
teach.narration: Because sixty-four is four cubed, flipping one quarter upside down with a negative power gives one quarter to the minus three, so this log is minus three.

teach.title: Evaluate bottom log
teach.narration: Eighty-one is three to the fourth power, so its reciprocal one over eighty-one is three to the minus four, giving minus four.

teach.title: Subtract negative number carefully
teach.narration: Watch the double minus sign in the numerator: three minus negative three becomes three plus three, which is six.

teach.title: Divide and simplify
teach.narration: Divide six by minus four and cancel two from top and bottom to get minus three over two.

teach.title: Final value
teach.narration: The value of the expression is minus three over two.

steps.title: Read prism dimensions
steps.narration: From the diagram, hypotenuse R S is five centimetres, base leg R T is four centimetres, and prism length O R is eight centimetres.

steps.title: Find missing leg ST
steps.narration: Use Pythagoras' theorem in right triangle R S T to find that the vertical leg S T is three centimetres.

steps.title: Area of triangular end
steps.narration: Calculate the triangular cross-sectional area using half times four times three to get six square centimetres.

steps.title: Volume of prism
steps.narration: Multiply the cross-sectional area six by the length eight to get forty-eight cubic centimetres.

teach.display: RS = OP = 5 cm, RT = 4 cm, OR = 8 cm
teach.title: Read diagram labels
teach.narration: Read the congruent right-triangular ends: hypotenuse R S equals O P at five centimetres, leg R T is four centimetres, and prism length O R is eight centimetres.

teach.title: Apply Pythagoras' theorem
teach.narration: Because angle R T S is ninety degrees, use Pythagoras' theorem on triangle R T S to find the missing leg S T.

teach.title: Calculate height ST
teach.narration: Subtract sixteen from twenty-five to get nine, then take the positive square root to get three centimetres.

teach.title: Find end area
teach.narration: The area of the right-angled triangular end is half base times height: half of four times three equals six square centimetres.

teach.title: Multiply area by length
teach.narration: For any prism, multiply the uniform cross-sectional area by its length eight centimetres.

teach.title: Volume of prism
teach.narration: The volume of the triangular prism is forty-eight cubic centimetres.
